highlights.title: Meta tweaks AI glasses to block some creepy recordings, but privacy risks remain
highlights.summary: Meta is rolling out an obvious fix to make its AI glasses less creepy amid backlash over the glasses' non-consensual recordings that have flooded the Internet. On Friday, The Verge reported that Meta closed a loophole that made it easy for smart-glasses users to cover up an LED light that is…
body: In a post on Threads, Meta’s executive vice president of wearables, Alex Himel, explained that an update would be rolled out soon that ensures that “the camera will now stop working if the light is covered during a recording.” That way “the capture LED can reliably alert bystanders when photos or videos are being captured for someone’s gallery,” Himel said.

According to Himel, “only a tiny minority of people try to get around these protections, and the fact they have to go to these lengths shows our efforts are working. We’ll keep improving and evolving our approach.”

However, bad actors may still be able to mod the glasses or tamper with the light without impacting recordings. And it’s unclear if popular bypasses, like using semi-transparent stickers that make the light less noticeable, would block recording under Meta’s new safeguard.

highlights.title: Anthropic gets its first court win over the Pentagon’s supply chain risk label
highlights.summary: A federal judge ruled the Trump administration illegally labeled Anthropic a supply chain risk, handing the AI company a victory as its second Pentagon lawsuit continues in Washington.
body: A federal judge in California ruled on Thursday evening that the Trump administration’s designation of Anthropic as a supply chain risk was illegal.

U.S. District Judge Rita Lin said in her ruling that Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth’s labeling of Anthropic as a risk to national security signified “unlawful retaliation” in violation of the First Amendment, and said the decision was “arbitrary and capricious.” Lin also said Anthropic was denied due process, as required under the Fifth Amendment.
Earlier this year, Hegseth and President Donald Trump labeled Anthropic a supply-chain risk and ordered all federal agencies, even those outside of defense, to stop working with the Claude maker.

The dispute stemmed from Anthropic setting hard lines on certain safety guardrails that would allow the Pentagon to use its models for fully autonomous weapons and mass surveillance of American citizens. The Pentagon denied that it would use Anthropic models for anything but lawful purposes, and alleged that Anthropic could try to control the military’s use of the models it bought and paid for.

highlights.title: Meta executive leaves for OpenAI as the social media giant faces growing scrutiny in India
highlights.summary: Sandhya Devanathan will oversee some OpenAI operations across Southeast Asia and Australia in her new role.
body: Meta’s India and Southeast Asia vice president, Sandhya Devanathan, is leaving the social media giant to join OpenAI, the ChatGPT maker told TechCrunch.

Devanathan will be based in Singapore and report to OpenAI’s Asia-Pacific managing director, Kiran Mani. She will oversee consumer growth, enterprise adoption and partnerships, regulatory engagement and operations across Southeast Asia and Australia, OpenAI said.

The executive is leaving Meta after more than a decade at the company, which has been the subject of growing scrutiny over issues such as online safety and content moderation. Devanathan was involved in the company’s decision process in the country, a person familiar with the matter said.
Devanathan’s appointment comes days after Prabhjeet Singh joined OpenAI as its India head. Singh had spent more than a decade at Uber, where he led its India and South Asia business.

highlights.title: Hell Let Loose: Vietnam review
highlights.summary: The most surprising thing about Hell Let Loose: Vietnam is how much DNA it shares with Big Walk. They both frequently involve traversing large expanses of terrain. They both have excellent maps. Most of all, they're both fundamentally games about communication.
body: The difference is in how they encourage chatty players. Big Walk gently coaxes players out of their shells through the medium of ingenious puzzles and good vibes. Hell Let Loose: Vietnam forces you to chat with your random squadmates because if you don't you're going to get bombed to shit. Where Big Walk is all carrot, Hell Let Loose: Vietnam is all stick, and it will not hesitate to thwack you with it if you don't play by the rules.

Grappling with Hell Let Loose: Vietnam can be an intimidating experience. But while its teaching style is much harsher, it does yield rewards. When Hell Let Loose: Vietnam comes together—with dozens of players working in tandem to overcome the enemy—the resulting show is utterly captivating. Unfortunately, it doesn't come together quite often enough to justify the pain of getting to that point.

highlights.title: Resident Evil 4 Remake ‘Chapter 0’ Released to Bring Back Cut Content
highlights.summary: Capcom’s Resident Evil 4 remake took a fairly ambitious approach to updating this classic. The game reworked several sequences, toned down the original’s escort mission woes, and added the ability to parry a chainsaw, which was quite neat.
body: It seems the remake was originally supposed to have even more Ashley-specific segments. Data miners found evidence of a scrapped prologue chapter which follows Ashley as she flees from her pursuers the night before Leon arrives in the village. While Capcom never completed the sequence, a modder combined the leftover pieces of this "Chapter 0" with existing in-game assets to create a playable version available on NexusMods.

In the mod, Ashley uses her phone as a flashlight while navigating the village at night. After witnessing the cultists murder an outsider, she also sees Luis being captured. The modder provides a detailed breakdown of what was restored, recreated, and added from the game files. Essentially, most of the animations, camera angles, and unique features, like Ashley’s phone flashlight, were from the game’s files. Everything else was stitched together from existing assets. The mod seamlessly integrates the prologue to play after the game’s opening cutscene and before Chapter 1.

highlights.title: AI Has Human Doctors Asking: What’s Left for Us?
highlights.summary: A recent paper argues that AI is often better at doctoring than doctors. Guess who isn't thrilled.
body: Don’t be fooled by the question mark in the title of an article published this month in the Journal of the American Medical Association. When the authors, including medical superstar Ezekiel Emanuel and venture capitalist Vinod Khosla, asked, “ Will Autonomous AI Exceed AI-Physicians as the Best Medical Care? ” they were being rhetorical. Their answer is an emphatic YES. Many in the medical world are begrudgingly coming to terms with the premise that patients can get the best treatment by a hybrid approach where doctors work in consultation with well-trained bots. But this article’s thesis is that AI alone can deliver the best outcomes.

highlights.title: Anthropic was illegally blacklisted by the Trump administration, court rules
highlights.summary: On Thursday, a judge ruled that the Pentagon's blacklisting of Anthropic earlier this year was unconstitutional, delivering the AI lab a win in a monthslong rollercoaster of a battle with the Trump administration.
body: The lawsuit, filed in March in a California district court, accused the Trump administration of unlawfully retaliating against Anthropic for setting “red lines,” or unacceptable military use cases of its AI technology.

“The empty invocation of national security is not a blank check to punish and retaliate against government critics,” Judge Rita F. Lin, a district judge in the northern district of California, wrote in the ruling.

She also wrote that the actions were “unlawful retaliation in violation of the First Amendment,” adding that Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth’s decision to designate Anthropic a supply chain risk “was arbitrary and capricious. Though the Department of War is undisputedly free to select the AI vendor of its choice, the evidence demonstrates that the broad measures imposed on Anthropic were illegal and baseless.”

body: He said he was "surprised how upset people were" about Sony ending support for physical game discs. Willits said he hasn't bought a physical game "in a long time" because he enjoys the convenience of digital games. Willits is not alone, as the share of digital game sales is growing at numerous companies.

At the same time, Sony continues to sell millions of physical game discs annually. Willits said Saber still makes "a lot of money" from physical games, especially in Europe, but the trends are different in North America, he observed.

Willits went on to say he had an interaction with someone recently who asked him to sign a copy of Doom 3, a game he worked on when he was with id Software. "So for me personally, I'll miss that in the future," he said.
Part of what many people enjoy about physical games is collecting the boxes they come in and presenting them on their shelves.

highlights.title: A Judge Has Blocked the Pentagon’s Attempt to Blacklist Anthropic
highlights.summary: A federal judge has called the Department of Defense’s designation of Anthropic as a national security supply-chain risk “illegal and baseless.”
body: A federal judge on Thursday barred the Trump administration from designating Anthropic a national security risk over a dispute about the use of its AI models, ruling that the designation amounted to unconstitutional retaliation.

The decision handed down by US district judge Rita Lin in California vacated the February 27 decision by defense secretary Pete Hegseth to label Anthropic a “supply-chain risk” and make the company ineligible for federal contracts. The ruling also lifted an additional punitive measure by Hegseth that prevented contractors or suppliers to the US military from doing business with Anthropic, a position Lin called “arbitrary, capricious, an abuse of discretion, and otherwise not in accordance with law.”

“Though the Department of War is undisputedly free to select the AI vendor of its choice, the evidence demonstrates that the broad measures imposed on Anthropic were illegal and baseless,” Lin wrote in a 59-page ruling.

The judge also ruled that nine agencies—including the Pentagon, the Treasury Department, the State Department, and the Department of Homeland Security—had improperly imposed sanctions on Anthropic. The ruling removes those penalties.

highlights.title: Gears Of War: E-Day Has A Battle Royale-Inspired PvP Mode Where You Can Strip The Flesh Off Enemies
highlights.summary: Gears of War games have had some of the best multiplayer action around ever since the days of the first game, and for Gears of War: E-Day, developers at The Coalition are looking to give fans plenty of options for online fun.
body: "It's very obviously inspired by battle royale games, but it's on a Gear-sized PVP map," creative director Matt Searcy said to GameSpot. "At the beginning of the map, there's lots of mobility, teams are moving around, you're trading the Power Core back and forth. But as the map goes on, you see defensive teams start to build up a front around the player they're protecting. And then, in awesome Gears fashion, the thing you're going to hold puts you at a slight disadvantage. So we gave you a heavy weapon that's basically a giant battery pack, and if somebody gets close to you within a really tight range, you can strip all the flesh off their body with a charge attack."

Crucible is one of four PvP modes that will be available on launch day. The multiplayer options include traditional Team Deathmatch, Conquest, and Demolition, each of which has been reworked for E-Day. Team Deathmatch has a dynamic respawn system to move spawn locations closer to where fights are breaking out, Conquest puts its own spin on the classic King of the Hill experience, and Demolition revolves around teams planting bombs on enemy territory.

highlights.title: How have my plants fared this summer? Some better than others
highlights.summary: It’ll soon be autumn, but the record-breaking weather has taken its toll on my vegetables. I’ve grown plants in heatwaves before, but this year has been different. Back-to-back heatwaves feel far more intense than the shorter ones I’m used to.
body: You might think more sun equals more growth, but that isn’t necessarily the case. When under heat stress, plants close their stomata – the pores on the underside of their leaves – hindering the movement of water and exchange of gases needed for photosynthesis. This can result in a check on growth that I’ve seen in several of my plants, some of which dropped their flowers before they could start bearing fruit.

Stressed-out plants can be vulnerable to pest attacks, which might explain why so many leaf miners have found my chard this year. Even some established perennials have struggled in the heat. The golden raspberries, which are in their second season, had canes that were growing well then suddenly turned brown and died.

highlights.title: Supporting Thailand’s next generation of AI startups
highlights.summary: OpenAI and Thailand’s MHESI launch an eight-week accelerator helping 10 health, wellness, and education startups turn AI prototypes into trusted products.
body: OpenAI and Thailand’s Ministry of Higher Education, Science, Research and Innovation are launching an eight-week accelerator to help startups turn promising ideas into products ready for real-world use.

Today in Bangkok, OpenAI and Thailand’s Ministry of Higher Education, Science, Research and Innovation (MHESI) announced a new accelerator to help Thai startups turn promising prototypes into products ready for real-world use and growth.

The OpenAI x MHESI AI Accelerator brings together ten startups working across health, wellness, and education. It marks OpenAI’s first public-private partnership with the Thai government focused on supporting local startups, and is being delivered with partners including the National Innovation Agency (NIA), Mahidol University, and Techsauce.

A compelling AI demonstration is only the beginning. Building a product that people can rely on is much harder. It takes careful testing, feedback from real users, strong safeguards, and a business model that can support the product as it grows. That work matters even more in healthcare and education, where the stakes are high and reliability is essential.

NBA 2K27 is making a pretty convincing case that this year's biggest changes aren't about finding one overpowered move and spamming it until my opponent rage-quits. The offensive side of the ball gets new toys including step-through up-and-unders, a Dynamic Layup Engine and expanded dribbling customisation, giving me more control over how I create space and attack the rim.

Defence isn't parking its arse on the bench either. Hands-up defence has been redesigned, the shot contest system has been overhauled, defensive cutoffs have been expanded and a new collision system should give physical play more weight. In other words, NBA 2K27 is trying to make both ends of the court count, which sounds like good news for anyone who has ever watched a teammate sprint towards the three-point line and decide defence is somebody else's problem.

highlights.title: How Does Harry Styles’s Madison Square Garden Show Grow?
highlights.summary: Harry, Harry, quite contrary, how does your (Madison Square) Garden grow? With disco balls and dance halls and screaming girls all in their rows.
body: Harry Styles first played Madison Square Garden at 18, as a heartthrob in a little pop quintet called One Direction. In 2012, he was fresh off Britain’s The X Factor and, not long before that, working the counter at W Mandeville Bakery in his native village of Holmes Chapel. He had a name—and an impish smile—ripe for stardom and a taste for skinny jeans. Arriving at the venue, he kissed the floor and marveled: “I made it to Madison Square Garden.”
These days, “I wouldn’t be caught dead kissing the floor with my pathetic immune system,” Styles told the crowd. “However, it is not lost on me what it means to play here.”

highlights.title: The Witcher 3: Songs of the Past – Geralt of Rivia returns after a decade in the sun
highlights.summary: Before The Witcher 4 arrives in 2028, CD Projekt Red is returning us to the world of The Witcher 3 for one last foray. Looks like wind’s still howlin’ The game that graced us with Bathtub Geralt, The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt, arrived more than a decade ago.
body: As it turns out, this is all possible thanks to a partnership with Fool’s Theory, a studio founded by CD Projekt Red veterans, which took on the brunt of the development work. “We’ve had this story in a drawer for many years,” explains Marcin Blacha, VP story director at CD Projekt Red. “Of course, we moved on to Cyberpunk 2077 and now The Witcher 4, as well as our other projects. But because we knew The Witcher 4 would take time, we saw a gap in our release calendar where Songs of the Past could go. Thankfully, we were able to find the right partner to help execute it.”

The elephant in the room, though, is that The Witcher 3’s 2016 expansion Blood and Wine felt like a natural conclusion to Geralt’s tale. After decades covered in entrails, the legendary monster slayer hangs up his dual swords for a well-earned life of luxury on his recently acquired vineyard estate. What can he possibly have left to do?
“That is certainly something we thought through,” says Blacha. “Geralt retired in Toussaint – but then his best friend comes calling. I don’t think many of us would turn down that request.”
